item.description: ### Changed - The arrow between two folders in the address bar points down while its menu of subfolders is open, as in Explorer, and is a little larger.

### Fixed - New Tab (⌘T) while a window shows a message, such as a path the address bar can't find, could make Treewise quit. A window that shows a message takes no new tab and is not put beside another until the message is answered, as on every Mac.

### Added - Refresh (⌘R) in the toolbar reads the folder again. - A details pane at the right of the window (View > Show Details, ⇧⌘P, or Details in the command bar): a Quick Look preview and the selection's kind, size, date and folder, or the count and total size of several items. - The address bar on a row of its own under the tab bar, as in Explorer: the path as buttons that take drops, a menu of the subfolders behind each arrow, and a field to type a path in (click its empty part or press ⌘L) that suggests folder names once typing pauses. The path bar at the bottom is gone. - The command bar is a row under the address bar, as in Explorer: New, the actions, Sort and View menus with a label, and Window Beside; in a narrow window the buttons show only their icons. The view buttons left the toolbar for the View menu and the status bar. - The status bar shows the item count at the left and icon buttons for List and Icons at the right, as in Explorer. - A click on the name of the selected item renames it after a short wait, as in Finder and Explorer, in the list and in the icon view.
### Changed - Tabs are macOS's window tabs: ⌘T and the + button open one, a tab tears off into its own window and Window > Merge All Windows joins them, as in Finder. ⌃⇥ shows the next tab. A file can no longer be dropped on a tab. - After a restart every window comes back with its tabs, each with its folder, sort order and view; before, only the window that changed last did. - Cut in one window and paste in another moves the items, as between tabs. - Split view is gone: Window > Window Beside (⌥⌘N) opens a second window and puts the two on the halves of the screen, as two Explorer windows. Open in Other Window, ⌥-double-click and ⌥⌘↓ open a folder in the most recently active other window, and the double-click setting chooses between this window and the other one. - Edit > Copy to Other Window and Move to Other Window, also in the context menu, copy or move the selection into the folder of the other window, with undo. - Undo and Redo are shared by all windows, as in Finder: ⌘Z in any window undoes the last move, copy, rename, new folder or trash, also after a drag from one window to another. - A window can't be made so narrow that the folder no longer fits beside the sidebar.
### Fixed - New Window (⌘N) opens a second window; in 0.2.0 Treewise quit. The toolbar can no longer be customized.

### Added - A command bar in the toolbar, as in Windows 11 File Explorer: New Folder, Cut, Copy, Paste, Rename, Share and Move to Trash. The toolbar can be customized. - Help > Treewise Website opens the download page.
### Fixed - A click on empty space in a pane, below its last row, makes that pane the active one.

### Fixed - Check for Updates… can be chosen; in 0.1.1 it stayed disabled. The setting for checking automatically shows whether it is on. - Installing with Homebrew no longer warns about deprecated forms in the cask.

The first beta: Treewise browses, copies and moves like Windows Explorer, signed and notarized so it opens without a warning.
### Added - A disk image to install from: drag Treewise into Applications. Started from elsewhere, Treewise offers once to move itself there. - Updates through Sparkle: Check for Updates… in the Treewise menu, and a daily check that can be turned off in Settings. - Copying and moving by dragging onto the list, the sidebar, a tab, the path bar or empty space, with a "Move to"/"Copy to" badge that follows ⌥ and ⌘; dragging to and from Finder, and from Mail and other apps that drag promised files. - Cut, copy and paste, also through the system pasteboard; ⌥⌘V moves what ⌘C copied. New folder, inline rename and Move to Trash, all undoable. - A conflict dialog with Replace, Keep Both and Stop, and Apply to All. - A progress panel for long transfers, in bytes and naming the file being copied, with Pause, Resume and Stop, also inside a large file. - An icon view with thumbnails beside the list (⌘1 and ⌘2), Quick Look with Space, and context menus. - Keyboard shortcuts for tabs, panes, opening and searching, listed in the README; split view is ⌥⌘\. Settings has a button to System Settings, where any menu item can get a key of its own. - Settings (⌘,): hidden files, file extensions, row size, the start folder, and where a double-clicked folder opens. - The last window's panes, tabs, sort order and view come back after a restart. - The app icon. - Browsing the disk on macOS: a sidebar with Favorites and a Locations tree from This Mac, tabs per pane, split view with two panes, a sortable list (Name, Date Modified, Size, Kind), a path bar and a status bar; folders update live when their contents change. - Dutch and German, following the system language. - The core model and rules: drag move-or-copy, "copy" names for conflicts, per-tab history, tabs and split panes, sorting, and date, size and kind formatting.
